fit: coffee history and current mental fatigue in two related Parkinson cases
assessment: Table 1 gives premorbid eight cups in case 1 and two to three cups in case 2. Current mental fatigue was 10.5 versus 10 out of 44. Preparation, timing and disease differences leave the exposure effect unresolved.

fit: fresh-derived rosemary extract-hydrolat and acute Bond–Lader mood
assessment: In healthy adults without a depression diagnosis, descriptive contentedness change was 4.30 versus 4.12 on plain water. Separate within-arm tests do not establish a difference. It has no depression scale and belongs to the 2023 ERP and 2025–2026 reporting family.

fit: carbonated rosemary extract and hydrolat beverage with affect outcomes
assessment: A 20-person healthy pilot gives exploratory positive and negative affect scores without significance tests or a depression scale. Equal calmness changes in the table contradict the narrative. Freshness of the leaves in this drink was unverified.

fit: fresh-derived rosemary beverage and fatigue or alertness in healthy adults
assessment: The randomized 80-person experiment measured post-task alertness and fatigue and describes very small unfavorable mood estimates. No nominal individual comparison survived correction. The full numeric mood table remains unverified, and depression was not measured.

fit: two rosemary species in oral capsules and acute energy or fatigue
assessment: The original reports an exploratory fatigue contrast with inconclusive treatment-by-time mood tests. The capsules combined two species and freshness or processing was unspecified. It gives no depression score.

fit: original aroma abstract with incomplete rosemary mood outcome
assessment: The author abstract attributes reported lower POMS depressed mood to lavender. Rosemary findings concern anxiety and alertness. Exact rosemary depressed-mood values in the full original are unverified. The route is inhaled aroma.

fit: rosemary polyphenols in the ICR mouse tail-suspension test
assessment: The primary abstract reports reduced immobility and neurotransmitter changes. The journal body remains gated, so preparation and experimental overlap with the Tsukuba dissertation are unverified.

fit: dried rosemary extract and murine immobility from a lab study described in a thesis
assessment: Figure 1-14 has lower tail-suspension immobility than water for both oral dried-leaf extract doses. The animal-level relationship to the same-laboratory Sasaki paper is unresolved. No clinical mood outcome was measured.

fit: Brazilian dried rosemary stem-and-leaf extract and mouse immobility
assessment: Acute and repeated extract exposure reduced immobility in swimming or suspension tests. Open-field locomotion showed no clear difference. A different laboratory and preparation from the Tsukuba studies; no fresh culinary or clinical depression comparison.

fit: dried-leaf tea and human peripheral biomarkers
assessment: In 22 healthy participants the author abstract reports higher BDNF and TNF-alpha after intake. It supplies no controlled clinical depression comparison or fresh leaf exposure.

fit: visual components among pooled hallucinosis and illusion reports
assessment: Of 129 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease, 32 reported hallucinosis or illusions and 30 of those reported a visual component. Episode rate and dried fig exposure were not measured.

fit: visual hallucinations during unrelated medication intoxication
assessment: The exact letter reports visual hallucinations during acute intoxication in an individual with parkinsonism. The food hypothesis and episode frequency are outside the report scope.

In the GBA case series Table 1 calls the presenting symptom rest tremor, while the prose reports no documented rest tremor at initial investigation. Neither case provides a raw fig or standardized rest-tremor severity contrast.

fit: dried rosemary extract and grooming behavior after olfactory bulbectomy in mice
assessment: Oral extract after olfactory bulbectomy shortened grooming latency and increased grooming time. The original distinguishes treatment-by-surgery effects from the inconclusive latency treatment main effect. The experiment assesses an indirect animal phenotype and does not establish a clinical depression result.

fit: registered three-extract pain trial with secondary depression measures
assessment: Overall between-group BDI-II p=.149; baseline BDI-II ≥4 subgroup p=.016. PROMIS depression comparison p=.798 and its within-group scoring interpretation is inconsistent with Methods. The rosemary, ashwagandha and sesame blend does not isolate fresh rosemary or a Parkinson effect.
